title: Fed decision in March?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's March 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for March 17 - 18, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their March meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket overwhelmingly favors no Federal Reserve rate change at the March 18-19 FOMC meeting, with 99.5% implied probability reflecting real capital backing amid robust economic data. The primary catalyst is January's blockbuster nonfarm payrolls surge of 256,000 jobs—far exceeding forecasts—coupled with steady 4.0% unemployment and core CPI inflation at 3.2% year-over-year, validating the Fed's patient stance after holding the 4.25%-4.50% target range steady in December. The dot plot projects just two 25bps cuts in 2025, likely starting mid-year. This positioning could face challenges from a downside surprise in February CPI data due February 12 or weakening labor indicators, potentially lifting 25bps cut odds above 1%, though such risks remain minimal per CME FedWatch alignment.

title: Netanyahu out by...?
description:

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket leans toward Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu remaining in office through 2024 and into 2025, driven by his coalition's recent passage of the 2025 state budget on September 30, which quelled ultra-Orthodox partners' threats of collapse and delayed snap election risks. Polls consistently show Netanyahu's Likud trailing opposition parties like National Unity by double digits, fueled by public frustration over the Gaza war, hostage negotiations, and judicial overhaul echoes. International factors, including stalled ICC arrest warrant proceedings and escalating Iran tensions, add uncertainty. Key watchpoints include Knesset no-confidence votes, potential war cabinet shifts, and November diplomatic deadlines that could fracture the fragile right-wing alliance.

title: 2026 FIFA World Cup Winner
description:
This market will resolve according to the national team that wins the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

If at any point it becomes impossible for this team to win the FIFA World Cup based on the rules of FIFA (e.g., they are eliminated in the knockout stage), this market will resolve immediately to “No”.

If the 2026 FIFA World Cup is permanently canceled or has not been completed by October 13, 2026, 11:59 PM this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source will be official information from FIFA, however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Spain's Euro 2024 victory has propelled them to the top of 2026 FIFA World Cup winner markets at 15.4%, highlighting their golden generation of talents like Lamine Yamal and Nico Williams amid cohesive play under Luis de la Fuente. England trails closely at 13.3% buoyed by Premier League depth and stars like Jude Bellingham, though final losses underscore finishing vulnerabilities. Argentina's 11.2% reflects Lionel Messi's enduring brilliance and Copa América retention, but an aging core tempers enthusiasm. Tight clustering stems from UEFA-CONMEBOL parity, volatile qualifiers—Brazil faltering, France potent—and the expanded 48-team format amplifying upsets, with trader consensus pricing in widespread contention among eight to ten elite national teams.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket's Republican Presidential Nominee 2028 market shows Robert F. Kennedy Jr. leading at 49%, ahead of J.D. Vance (39.3%) and Marco Rubio (26.5%), driven by early positioning among Trump allies in a wide-open post-term-limited GOP field. The tight race stems from shared loyalty to former President Trump—evident in RFK Jr.'s endorsement, Vance's vice presidential selection, and Rubio's secretary of state confirmation—yet differentiated strengths: RFK Jr.'s outsider health policy focus, Vance's populist Midwestern appeal, and Rubio's establishment foreign policy credentials. Developments like Trump's endorsements, administration role performances, or 2026 midterm outcomes could widen leads by signaling base support.
